thread_analysis.thread_summary: Over several months, [COMPANY] (a module manufacturer) works through a Bluetooth registration strategy for its own Controller Subsystem-registered module combined with a separately Component-registered Host stack (NXP RW610/RW612). The thread covers how to combine a module's Controller Subsystem registration with a Component-registered Host stack into an End-Product-equivalent registration, whether multiple same-module product variants can share one registration, an SIG-relayed explanation of why the post-July-2024 registration site requires Consistency Checking across the entire referenced Core Layer hierarchy (not just the new design portion, as before), and two techniques for eliminating lower-layer test requirements triggered by overlapping RF PHY/LL layers across combined registrations.
all_questions_found: Can a module's Controller Subsystem registration be combined directly with a separately Component-registered Host stack to produce an End Product registration, or is a different procedure needed?

Does a Component registration that includes lower-layer content (such as LL/RF PHY alongside the GATT stack) cause a conflict when referenced alongside the module's own Controller Subsystem, given the layer overlap?
Is RF testing exempted under this combined registration approach, and is profile testing required?
Can multiple product variants sharing the same module and host stack be registered under a single Host Subsystem DID?
Why does the current registration site require lower-layer (Core Layer) test items in scenarios where the pre-July-2024 Launch Studio system did not?
When two registrations to be combined both cover overlapping RF PHY and LL layers, does selecting the duplicate layers trigger a new test requirement, and how can this be avoided?
Can swapping one registration's RF PHY and LL layer content for another's matching content (within the Qualification Workspace) eliminate a lower-layer test trigger caused by layer overlap?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread covers combining a module's Controller Subsystem registration with a separately Component-registered Host stack: rather than a direct End-Product registration, a new Host Subsystem design registration is performed that combines/selects the Component-registered host stack together with the module's Controller Subsystem, carrying equivalent legal effect to an End Product registration, with RF testing exempted and profile testing required only for SIG-defined profiles; any unneeded overlapping layers (such as LL/RF PHY content bundled into a Host-stack Component registration) can be selectively excluded during this design registration process without issue. It also explains, per an SIG representative's own account, why the post-July-2024 registration site extended Consistency Checking to the entire referenced Core Layer hierarchy rather than just the new design portion (as Launch Studio did) -- because Core Spec v6.0 and later introduced scenarios where the old v4.0 LE lower-layer Mandatory feature set alone is insufficient, forcing the new system to check the full referenced hierarchy. Finally, it demonstrates two techniques for resolving a lower-layer test requirement triggered when two combined registrations have overlapping RF PHY/LL layers with identical underlying ICS: referencing only the broader, single registration that already covers the same ICS (dropping the narrower, redundant one), or substituting one registration's RF PHY/LL layer content for the other's matching content within the Qualification Workspace.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: A module's Controller Subsystem cannot be directly combined with a separately Component-registered Host stack to form an End Product registration; instead, a new Host Subsystem design registration referencing both, with selective layer inclusion to resolve any overlap, achieves equivalent effect with RF testing exempted. Multiple product variants sharing a module and host stack cannot share a single Host Subsystem DID directly, but can all be covered via the free, self-service Product List 'Add Product' mechanism after the initial registration. Lower-layer test requirements triggered by overlapping RF PHY/LL layers across two combined registrations can be avoided, when the overlapping ICS content is verified identical, either by referencing only the broader registration alone or by substituting the overlapping layer content between registrations in the Workspace -- both achieve the same ICS without requiring new testing.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Attempting to register an End Product directly from a Controller Subsystem and a Component-registered Host stack without going through the correct Host Subsystem design registration process would not produce a valid registration. Assuming overlapping layers between two combined registrations can simply be selected without consequence risks triggering an unplanned new lower-layer test requirement that existing test reports cannot satisfy as evidence, since the test items follow the current TCRL rather than the report's original vintage.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When combining a module's Controller Subsystem with a separately Component-registered Host stack, use the Host Subsystem design registration process (selectively excluding any overlapping layers) rather than attempting a direct End Product registration. Before referencing two registrations with overlapping RF PHY/LL layers, check whether their underlying ICS content is actually identical -- if so, either reference only the broader registration alone or substitute the overlapping layer content between them in the Workspace, both of which avoid a new lower-layer test requirement that current-TCRL test items would otherwise impose.
